title: 3-Year Treasury Note auction (January new issue) — 1:00pm ET Monday, the front leg of the compressed Mon/Tue/Wed January block
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes, PDF CreationDate D:20260804173209-04'00'), FlateDecode streams inflated per page and rows rebuilt from Tm coordinates. The page-3 row reads verbatim `3-Year  NOTE / Thursday, January 07, 2027 / Monday, January 11, 2027 / Friday, January 15, 2027`, carrying NO `R` against a page legend that reads `R --denotes reopening` — so this is a NEW ISSUE, unlike the 10-Year and 30-Year legs of the same block, which both carry `R`. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing coupon-auction convention and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2027-01-07 coupon announcement. Discovered in the never-assessed initial research of treasury-30y-bond-2027-01-13, 2026-09-09
notes: PROPOSED, NOT CANONICAL. Filed because the calendar tracks `treasury-3y-note-2026-09-08`, `-10-06`, `-11-09` and `-12-07` as first-class medium entries and then stops, leaving the entire January 2027 mid-quarter coupon block untracked apart from the two legs proposed alongside it. THE 3-YEAR IS ALWAYS A NEW ISSUE, which is what separates it from its two block-mates: zero of the 45 3-Year auctions since 2023-01-01 carry `reopening: Yes` (`api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov` auctions_query, pulled 2026-09-09), and every 3-Year row on the fetched schedule page — August 2026 through January 2027 — is printed without the `R` marker. So a January 3-Year creates a security; the January 10-Year and 30-Year sell more of one November created. SIZE NULL $58B, flat for 16 consecutive monthly auctions from 2025-06-10 through 2026-09-08, with the January prints running $40B (2023-01-10), $52B (2024-01-09), $58B (2025-01-06) and $58B (2026-01-12). The size is decided at the 2026-11-04 quarterly refunding, not at the 2027-01-07 announcement that publishes it. WHY MONDAY, and it is the same answer the proposing event's own Wednesday slot got: settlement is Friday 2027-01-15, and since 2017 no nominal coupon in this block has settled fewer than two business days after its auction, so the 30-Year is pinned to Wednesday 01-13 and the three legs run backwards from there as a contiguous Mon/Tue/Wed rather than the more common Tue/Wed/Thu. WHAT A LATER SESSION SHOULD ACTUALLY MEASURE HERE, left open deliberately: the 3-Year's SOMA add-on is enormous and bimodal in a way the long end's is not — $0.00B on 2025-09-09, 2025-12-08, 2026-03-10, 2026-06-09 and 2026-09-08, against $16.88B on 2026-01-12 and $16.43B on 2026-02-10 — so a headline offering size understates the January line by an amount no other leg of this block approaches. Reading it, not trading it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed.
